previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis, J-tube placement, and Nissen fundoplication was readmitted less than 24 hours after discharge due to recurrent nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Symptoms began after increasing her tube feed rate and were consistent with her usual gastroparesis flares. She received IV antiemetics, morphine, and fluids, with resolution of symptoms by the next day. Metabolic acidosis from dehydration improved with treatment, and electrolytes stabilized. She tolerated tube feeds at 90 mL/hr without further vomiting. The gastroenterology team concluded that diagnostic and therapeutic options are exhausted and recommended ongoing symptom management with tube feeds and PRN medications. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mrs. ___ is a ___ year old female with history of 
gastroparesis and multiple recent admissions for gastroparesis 
s/p J-tube placement ___, who presents with her typical 
symptoms of abdominal pain and vomiting. She had no evidence of 
small-bowel obstruction, no sign of infections, and electrolytes 
within normal limits. She was treated with morphine, Ativan, 
prochlorperazine, and Zofran, which is a regimen that has worked 
on previous admissions. She received 1 L IVF. The next day, she 
tolerated her regular tube feeds, and was discharged to home 
with follow up in place to see Dr. ___ at ___ who 
follows her gastroparesis.

#Gastroparesis/vomiting: She presented with no symptoms 
different from usual flair. There was no concern for SBO given 
benign exam and continued BMs. There were no signs of infection- 
she remained afebrile, no elevated WBC. She's had more frequent 
flares over the last several months thought to be due to rate of 
tube feeds, however this flare occured at a lower rate (68 vs 
90). Unknown etiology of gastroparesis (no DM, no infiltrative 
malignancy, no vagal nerve injury). She was discharged to home 
after tolerating clears and tube feeds overnight. She is 
followed at ___ by Dr. ___ has an appointment in 2 weeks.
.

was continued while in the hospital.
